rep.angle: lead with a recent hiring push you noticed
rep.name: Maya

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Dana, Maya from HyperSale. I noticed Brightpath’s recent sales hiring push—may I take 30 seconds to explain why I’m calling?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks. Gong shows managers what happened after calls; HyperSale lets new reps practice realistic buyers beforehand, with quote-backed scoring. How are you ramping hires today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already have Gong for this. Why would I add another platform to the stack?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That makes sense—Gong reviews real calls; HyperSale creates safe repetitions before prospects are affected. Where does Gong leave gaps in ramping those new hires?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Fair. New hires are still getting most of their practice on live prospects, which isn’t ideal for ramp. But my managers don’t have time for another tool.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Exactly—HyperSale replaces manager-led roleplays with AI practice and quote-backed scoring, so managers review progress, not sessions. How many hours weekly does coaching consume?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Honestly, very few—that’s the problem. Managers rarely listen to Gong recordings, and coaching usually happens after a deal is already lost, so how does this avoid becoming another dashboard they ignore?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s the risk. HyperSale surfaces week-over-week practice progress with exact quotes, so what does delayed coaching cost you in lost deals or ramp time?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That’s hard to isolate—pipeline coverage and attach rate move for a dozen reasons. How would I measure whether the practice itself improves ramp, versus reps simply completing exercises?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: In a 30-day pilot, we’d baseline one cohort, correlate quote-backed skill gains with Gong outcomes, and separate improvers from completers. Which milestone matters most?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Time to first qualified opportunity is probably the cleanest ramp milestone, with stage-one-to-two conversion as a guardrail. But we just renewed Gong for two years, and there’s no budget for another platform this year.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Understood—this complements Gong; annual pricing is $90 per rep monthly. What must a one-team, 30-day pilot prove to earn next year’s budget?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: You didn’t answer the budget point. Unless you’re proposing a one-team pilot under my $15k approval limit, this doesn’t go anywhere this year.
